newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods mixed amid confusion on diesel.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods mixed amid confusion on diesel.

text.p: Prices of U.S. spot oil products were mixed late Monday tracking slightly firmer NYMEX gasoline and weaker heating oil futures, players said, with ultra-thin trade amid confusion over true valuations for low sulfur diesel.
Although heating oil differentials held steady, diffs on other distillates ended mostly firmer, moved by the occasional deal.

"It's a screwy market. Nobody's pushing for volume so it's easy to move prices," one Gulf trader said, adding distillates seemed overvalued given the API's estimate of record-high U.S. production of 3.8 million barrels per day for recent weeks.
"Most of what we produce is low sulfur diesel, but despite increasing supplies prices are going up," he said, giving Gulf low sulfur diesel a four cent premium to heating oil.

"In the Gulf, at this time of year, the premium is usually closer to a penny or inside a penny," he added, adding that a two-million-barrel low sulfur diesel build last week moved total U.S. stocks 421,000 barrels ahead of last year's levels.
